paragraphs.source_en: The interpretation advanced here will hopefully change the rules in the study of the Central Saharan rock art, where the search for the meaning has always been avoided as something undesirable and impossible. It is evident that using the combination of ethnographic record, comparative studies and archaeology, an interpretation can be attempted and can bring significant results. Some ideas were proposed for the first time, such as the existence of "rain animals" based on the comparative study with the South African rock art. Another similarity between the San rock art and the Round Heads was examined, namely the predominance of antelope and mouflon over other animal species represented. Their images are concentrated especially on the Tassili Plateau which does not follow the complete distribution of these quadrupeds in the region, as attested by excavations in the lower mountains.

paragraphs.source_en: It emerges clearly that the description and classification of the paintings cannot remain the only approach in the study of the Saharan rock art. Innovative approaches must be undertaken in order to advance the research of the Round Head paintings; only if new hypothesis are introduced and tested can we learn something about the ideology and the spiritual world of these complex populations. One of the most promising fields of research is the systematic study of the landscape. Not only should the painted sites be examined in relation to their environment in an effort to understand the pattern of their selection but also non-painted sites should be investigated in order to clarify why they were not selected for image-making. Regarding the painted sites, direct dating and excavations are desperately needed as they are the only way to determine the cultures and the possible use of the sites.
